record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: Does the Continuum Hypothesis imply that there exists a subgroup G ≤ Z^N of size c satisfying the Borel γ-property S1(BΩ, BΓ), or at least the open-cover γ-property S1(Ω, Γ)?

evidence.quote: Does the Continuum Hypothesis imply the existence of a group G ≤ ZN of cardinality c satisfying S1(BΩ, BΓ), or at least S1(Ω, Γ)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}$ denote the Baer–Specker group, i.e., the topological group of all integer sequences with pointwise addition, endowed with the product topology (each copy of $\mathbb{Z}$ being discrete). For a topological space $X$:

- An open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is an $\omega$-cover if $X \notin \mathcal{U}$ and every finite subset of $X$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{U}$.
- An open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is a $\gamma$-cover if it is infinite and every $x \in X$ belongs to all but finitely many members of $\mathcal{U}$.
- Let $\Omega$ (resp. $\Gamma$) denote the family of all open $\omega$-covers (resp. open $\gamma$-covers) of $X$.
- A countable Borel cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is a Borel $\omega$-cover if every finite subset of $X$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{U}$, and a Borel $\gamma$-cover if every $x \in X$ is in all but finitely many members. Let $\mathcal{B}_\Omega$ (resp. $\mathcal{B}_\Gamma$) denote the families of countable Borel $\omega$-covers (resp. $\gamma$-covers).
- For families $\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}$ of covers, $S_1(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B})$ is the selection principle: for every sequence $(U_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with $U_n \in \mathcal{A}$, one can choose $u_n \in U_n$ such that $\{u_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \in \mathcal{B}$.

Question: Assuming the Continuum Hypothesis, does there exist a subgroup $G \leq \mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}$ of cardinality $\mathfrak{c}$ (with the subspace topology) such that $G$ satisfies $S_1(\mathcal{B}_\Omega, \mathcal{B}_\Gamma)$? Failing that, must there at least exist such a subgroup satisfying $S_1(\Omega, \Gamma)$?

artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published resolution of this specific question about CH yielding a size-$\mathfrak{c}$ subgroup of the Baer–Specker group satisfying $S_1(\mathcal{B}_\Omega, \mathcal{B}_\Gamma)$ or $S_1(\Omega, \Gamma)$. Related work on Menger-bounded subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}$ under CH exists, but no source confirms a solution to this particular problem; the current status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: Squares of Menger-bounded groups
status_evidence.snippet: Under CH, there is a Menger-bounded subgroup of the Baer–Specker group whose square is not Menger-bounded.
status_evidence.claim: Related CH constructions of special subgroups of Z^N exist, but the specific S_1(B_Omega, B_Gamma) / S_1(Omega, Gamma) question is not addressed here.

status_evidence.title: Baer–Specker group - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Baer–Specker group is the direct product of countably many copies of Z.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference for the ambient group; no resolution of the selection-principle question stated.
